newsitem.title: BELARUS: Belarus parliament defies president on referendum.
newsitem.headline: Belarus parliament defies president on referendum.

text.p: The Belarus parliament, setting itself on a collision course with President Alexander Lukashenko, decided on Friday to go ahead with a referendum on November 24 that could abolish the post of president.
Deputies voted by 88 to 84 in favour of carrying out their poll shortly after Lukashenko stormed out of parliament vowing to hold a separate referendum designed to extend his mandate.

The 41-year-old Lukashenko, who has been accused by critics of taking an increasingly authoritarian line since coming to power two years ago, told parliament he had withdrawn proposals intended to appease deputies opposed to his poll.
He reaffirmed his resolve to go ahead with the November 7 referendum on a new constitution which would give him a new five-year tenure into the next century.
"I will go directly to the people and I will withdraw my initiative, and the people will be our judge," he said.
Some deputies and the constitutional court had warned that Lukashenko's referendum would divide the ex-Soviet republic and could lead to the establishment of a dictatorship.
